quests.instruction: Mia just finished eating dinner at the table. Now she wants to relax on the sofa and watch her favorite show. Which room is she walking into?
quests.question: Living Room
quests.hint: This room has a sofa and a television for relaxing together.
quests.explanation: That's right! The Living Room has a sofa and television, perfect for relaxing after dinner.
quests.funFact: Many families spend their evenings together in the living room after a meal.

quests.instruction: Before Dad can bake a cake, he needs an appliance that surrounds the batter with heat on every side. Which appliance does he turn on?
quests.question: Oven
quests.hint: This appliance has a door and bakes food evenly all around, not just on top.
quests.explanation: Yes! An oven surrounds food with heat on every side, perfect for baking a cake.
quests.funFact: The whole house often smells sweet while a cake bakes inside the oven.

quests.instruction: After playing in the garden, Sam's hands are covered in dirt. Which room should he visit first to wash them clean?
quests.question: Bathroom
quests.hint: This room has a sink where you can wash your hands with soap and water.
quests.explanation: Correct! The Bathroom has a sink for washing dirty hands clean after playing outside.
quests.funFact: Washing your hands well helps keep away germs after playing outdoors.

quests.instruction: Grandma wants to read quietly and keep her books organized nearby. Which piece of furniture would help her the most?
quests.question: Bookshelf
quests.hint: This furniture has flat shelves where books stand in a neat row.
quests.explanation: That's right! A bookshelf keeps books organized in neat rows, perfect for a quiet reader.
quests.funFact: A tall bookshelf can hold dozens of favorite stories at once.

quests.instruction: It is nighttime, and Leo wants his room dark so he can fall asleep. Which item should he pull shut across his window?
quests.question: Curtains
quests.hint: This soft fabric hangs beside a window and can be pulled closed.
quests.explanation: Yes! Curtains can be pulled shut across a window to block out light at night.
quests.funFact: Curtains can be opened wide for sunshine or closed for a cozy, dark room.

quests.instruction: A guest is arriving soon, and Mom wants them to be able to announce their arrival without knocking loudly. Which small object does she make sure is working?
quests.question: Doorbell
quests.hint: Pressing this object makes a sound to tell everyone a visitor has arrived.
quests.explanation: Correct! A doorbell lets a guest announce their arrival with a simple ring or chime.
quests.funFact: A doorbell means nobody has to wait by the window to see who arrived.

quests.instruction: Dad parks the car safely for the night before locking up the house. Which room did he just walk out of?
quests.question: Garage
quests.hint: This room is where the family car stays safe overnight.
quests.explanation: That's right! Dad parks the car in the garage before locking up for the night.
quests.funFact: Many garages have a big door that opens wide enough for a car to drive through.

quests.instruction: The Alvarez family invited someone who lives far away to come eat dinner and sleep over in the spare room for the night. What do we call this visitor?
quests.question: Guest
quests.hint: This word describes someone who is visiting and staying over, not someone who lives there every day.
quests.explanation: Correct! A guest is a visitor who comes to stay or share a meal at someone else's home.
quests.funFact: Families often keep an extra blanket ready in case a guest stays the night.

quests.instruction: Before Priya can watch her favorite cartoon, she walks into the room with both a television and a comfy sofa. Which room is this?
quests.question: Living Room
quests.hint: This room has both a television and a sofa for the whole family.
quests.explanation: Yes! The Living Room has a television and sofa, perfect for watching a favorite cartoon.
quests.funFact: A living room often has the comfiest seats in the whole house.

quests.instruction: Mom just bought fresh milk and vegetables at the store. Which appliance keeps them cold so they do not spoil before dinner?
quests.question: Refrigerator
quests.hint: This tall kitchen appliance has a door and keeps food chilled inside.
quests.explanation: That's right! A refrigerator keeps milk and vegetables cold and fresh until it is time to cook.
quests.funFact: Opening the refrigerator door for too long can let all the cold air out.

quests.instruction: Crumbs are scattered all over the rug after snack time. Which appliance would best clean them up?
quests.question: Vacuum Cleaner
quests.hint: This machine sucks up dust and crumbs from the rug and floor.
quests.explanation: Yes! A vacuum cleaner sucks up crumbs and dust to make the rug clean again.
quests.funFact: Many families vacuum their rugs and floors at least once every week.

quests.instruction: Smoke from the cozy fireplace needs somewhere to escape outside. Which part of the house lets it drift safely away?
quests.question: Chimney
quests.hint: This tall pipe rises up from the roof.
quests.explanation: Correct! A chimney lets smoke from a fireplace escape safely up and away from the house.
quests.funFact: Some homes have birds or squirrels that try to nest near the top of a chimney.

quests.instruction: Ben wants to keep his favorite book and a small lamp within reach while he lies in bed. Which piece of furniture should he place them on?
quests.question: Nightstand
quests.hint: This small table sits right beside the bed.
quests.explanation: That's right! A nightstand sits beside the bed, perfect for a lamp and a favorite book.
quests.funFact: Many people keep a lamp on their nightstand to read before falling asleep.

quests.instruction: Before cooking dinner, Mom checks the shelves where cans, rice, and pasta are stored. Which room is she looking inside?
quests.question: Pantry
quests.hint: This small room keeps dry food organized on shelves.
quests.explanation: Yes! A pantry stores cans, rice, and pasta neatly on shelves until it is time to cook.
quests.funFact: A pantry keeps food fresh and organized so it is easy to find later.

quests.instruction: The Kim family's new puppy loves to run around, so they want a barrier to keep it safely inside the yard. What should they build?
quests.question: Fence
quests.hint: This outdoor barrier runs along the edge of the yard.
quests.explanation: Correct! A fence keeps a puppy safely inside the yard while it plays and runs.
quests.funFact: A fence around a yard helps keep a family pet safely inside.

quests.instruction: Noah needs a quiet room with a desk and bookshelves to finish his homework without distractions. Which room fits this best?
quests.question: Study
quests.hint: This room is often the quietest place in the house, perfect for concentrating.
quests.explanation: That's right! A study has a desk and books, making it perfect for quiet homework.
quests.funFact: Some people call a study a home office, since grown-ups sometimes work there too.

quests.instruction: A big pile of dirty clothes is waiting to be cleaned before school starts again. Which appliance will wash them with soap and water?
quests.question: Washing Machine
quests.hint: This appliance spins and sloshes clothes around to get them clean.
quests.explanation: Yes! A washing machine spins dirty clothes around with soap and water to clean them.
quests.funFact: A washing machine spins clothes around quickly to squeeze out extra water.

quests.instruction: Grandpa is mailing a birthday card and needs to write down the exact numbers and street name of your home. What is he writing?
quests.question: Address
quests.hint: This is the numbers and street name that helps mail find your home.
quests.explanation: Correct! An address is the numbers and street name that help mail reach exactly the right home.
quests.funFact: Knowing your own address is a helpful thing for every child to learn.

quests.instruction: Standing behind a railing high above the ground, Layla enjoys the breeze and the view from her apartment. Which part of the home is she standing on?
quests.question: Balcony
quests.hint: This outdoor space is above the ground floor, with a railing for safety.
quests.explanation: That's right! A balcony is an outdoor space above the ground with a railing for safety.
quests.funFact: Many balconies have a railing to keep everyone safe while enjoying the view.

quests.instruction: Before school, Ana drops a slice of bread into a small appliance that will make it warm and crispy. Which appliance is she using?
quests.question: Toaster
quests.hint: This countertop appliance browns bread until it becomes crispy toast.
quests.explanation: Yes! A toaster browns a slice of bread until it becomes warm and crispy.
quests.funFact: Most toasters pop the bread back up once it is perfectly toasted.

quests.instruction: Before leaving for school, the whole family checks that this safety device on the front door is closed tight. What are they checking?
quests.question: Lock
quests.hint: This safety device only opens again with the right key.
quests.explanation: Correct! A lock keeps a door shut safely until it is opened again with the right key.
quests.funFact: Checking that the lock is closed is a good habit before leaving home.

quests.instruction: Toys, building blocks, and puzzles are spread across the floor while a group of kids play together. Which room are they most likely in?
quests.question: Playroom
quests.hint: This room is filled with toys and games just for playing.
quests.explanation: That's right! A playroom is filled with toys and games, perfect for kids to play together.
quests.funFact: Many families turn an extra room into a playroom just for the kids.

quests.instruction: Grandma wants to make a warm cup of tea, so she puts water into a pot with a spout to heat it up quickly. Which item is she using?
quests.question: Kettle
quests.hint: This pot heats water quickly and sometimes whistles when it is ready.
quests.explanation: Yes! A kettle heats water quickly, perfect for making a warm cup of tea.
quests.funFact: Some kettles whistle loudly the moment the water inside starts to boil.

quests.instruction: Every Saturday, Omar makes his bed and takes out the trash to help keep the home tidy. What do we call these small helpful jobs?
quests.question: Chore
quests.hint: This word describes a small, helpful job you do around the house.
quests.explanation: Correct! A chore is a small, helpful job around the house, like making your bed.
quests.funFact: Many families share chores so no single person has too many jobs to do.

quests.instruction: Plates, forks, and spoons are set on the table as the whole family gathers to eat a special birthday dinner. Which room are they in?
quests.question: Dining Room
quests.hint: This room has a big table where the whole family shares meals.
quests.explanation: That's right! A dining room has a big table for the family to share a special meal.
quests.funFact: A dining room table is often big enough for the whole family to sit together.

quests.instruction: Instead of a closet built into the wall, the Petrov family's new apartment has a tall standalone cabinet for hanging clothes. What is this piece of furniture called?
quests.question: Wardrobe
quests.hint: This piece of furniture stands on its own, with doors, unlike a space built into the wall.
quests.explanation: Yes! A wardrobe stands on its own, with doors that open to reveal a bar for hanging clothes.
quests.funFact: Long ago, before closets were built into walls, every home needed a wardrobe.

quests.instruction: Every afternoon, Grandpa checks the small box near the front of the house to see if any letters have arrived. What is he checking?
quests.question: Mailbox
quests.hint: This small box holds letters and packages until someone brings them inside.
quests.explanation: Correct! A mailbox holds letters and packages until someone brings them inside the house.
quests.funFact: Some mailboxes have a small flag you can raise to signal outgoing mail.

quests.instruction: Right after cutting up carrots for dinner, Dad rinses them clean under running water. Which fixture is he using?
quests.question: Sink
quests.hint: This fixture has a faucet with running water for washing food or hands.
quests.explanation: That's right! A sink has running water, perfect for rinsing vegetables clean before cooking.
quests.funFact: Kitchens and bathrooms both usually have their own sink for washing up.

quests.instruction: The living room floor felt cold and bare, so the family added something soft and colorful to cover part of it. What did they add?
quests.question: Rug
quests.hint: This soft covering makes a hard floor feel warmer underfoot.
quests.explanation: Yes! A rug is a soft, colorful covering that makes a hard floor feel warmer.
quests.funFact: Many families place a soft rug under the coffee table in the living room.

quests.instruction: In the Nguyen family's home, everyone shares meals, chores, and the same address together. What word describes this whole group living together?
quests.question: Household
quests.hint: This word means everyone who lives together, sharing one home.
quests.explanation: Correct! A household is everyone who lives together under one roof, sharing meals and chores.
quests.funFact: A household can be big or small, with just one person or many family members.
